newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat may up MGTI lines to 500,000.
newsitem.headline: Indosat may up MGTI lines to 500,000.

text.p: Indonesia's international telephone operator PT Indonesian Satellite Corporation (Indosat) said on Wednesday its fixed telephone unit is studying the possibility of installing 500,000 lines against a previous target of 400,000 in Java.
"MGTI is currently evaluating increasing its commitment from 400,000 lines to 500,000 lines," Indosat said in a statement.

Indosat unit PT Mitra Global Telekomunikasi Indonesia (MGTI) said last October it had secured a $480 million syndicated loan to develop 400,000 lines in Central Java and Jogjakarta and expected the project to be completed in March 1999.
The syndication was led by Australia and New Zealand Banking Group, Japan's Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd and Deutsche Bank AG's Deutshe Bank Asia Pacific.
MGTI shareholders other than Indosat include Australia's Telstra Global Limited and Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp. and Itochu Corp.
Indosat said MGTI expected to install 267,000 lines in 1997 and 108,000 lines in 1998.
Indosat, also listed in New York, did not give further details. Officials were not immediately available for comment.
